target_customer: Companies and organizations wanting an internal question and answer knowledge base for employees
problem: Knowledge inside companies is locked in people's heads and email threads. Opzi offered a Quora-style Q&A site for businesses so employees could ask and answer questions and keep the answers.
business_model: B2B SaaS for enterprise Q&A (pricing not found)

founders.name: Euwyn Poon
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2010-09-24) says he practiced law for two years after law school, firm not named.

founders.name: Benjamin Preston
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page only.

founders.name: Nathan Speller
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page only.

competitors.name: Yammer
competitors.what: Enterprise social network, which TechCrunch contrasted with Opzi as a knowledge base

technical_complexity.rationale: A Q&A site with company-private spaces was standard web engineering by a small team in 2010; no research-grade problem is described in the sources.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated internal answers could create some lock-in, but Q&A software was easy to copy and Jive and Yammer could add Q&A features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A 2010 ReadWrite snippet predicted that Jive and Yammer might add Q&A features. The outcome for Opzi was a transformation into the First Round Network per the YC page, not a documented takeover.

market_need_then: Enterprise social tools such as Yammer were gaining attention in 2010 and Quora was a rising consumer Q&A site, but the sources opened give no usage or revenue evidence for enterprise Q&A demand.

branding.domain_note: Used opzi.com; the site returned HTTP 503 when fetched in this research.

rebrands.why: The YC page says Opzi became the First Round Network; reason not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found only launch coverage and directory entries, no sign of brand traction or community.

pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page says Opzi became the First Round Network.

outcome_analysis: Opzi launched at TechCrunch Disrupt in September 2010 after raising about $1M from a prominent angel syndicate including First Round Capital and SV Angel. YC lists it as inactive and says it became the First Round Network. No post-mortem or shutdown date was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: The $1M figure is TechCrunch's 'nearly $1 million'; SeedTable reports $1.02M total. The seed $15K (2010-01) and the 2010-08-22 round rest on a single database (BounceWatch) and may be the YC deal. A ReadWrite article (readwrite.com/?p=80072, fetch blocked, search snippet only) names MindQuilt as a rival and calls Opzi a private beta, but its date could not be verified so it is not listed as a competitor. The TechCrunch article that supplied the Yammer comparison was seen only as a search snippet. Opzi site fetch returned 503.
